AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: Queen.cs:125-130 does exactly two things: caches `Amalgam = CombatState.Enemies.First(c => c.Monster is TorchHeadAmalgam)` and sets the 'queen_progress' music parameter to 1f. The music half is presentation (SHARED-FINDINGS section 4 waives NRunMusicController). The cache half is DEAD STATE in the source: `Amalgam` is written at Queen.cs:128 and nulled at :227 and is READ NOWHERE in the file -- every decision goes through HasAmalgamDied instead. The sim drops the field and resolves the amalgam live in _amalgam() whenever a condition needs it, which is the same observable. Note this is NOT the shared constructor-power finding: the Queen applies no starting power, so SHARED-FINDINGS section 2 does not apply and this entry stands on its own reading. One divergence the live lookup introduces and the cache does not: C#'s `.First(...)` THROWS if the encounter contains no amalgam, while the sim's loop returns None and _amalgam_died() then reports True, sending the Queen straight to OFF_WITH_YOUR_HEAD. Dormant on both sides -- QUEEN_BOSS is the Queen's only encounter and always pairs her with a TorchHeadAmalgam (queen.py:193-196), matching the C# boss.

AfterDeath.maps_to: Queen._burn_bright's substitution check (queen.py:166-179); there is no sim AfterDeath listener at all
AfterDeath.issue: THE UNCLAIMED HOOK OVERRIDE handed to the content tier by monster_state_machine boundary hole 5. Read to the END first, per the KinPriest N6 precedent, and it is NOT all presentation: Queen.cs:221-241 has a presentation shell (two NRunMusicController 'queen_progress' updates, a QUEEN.amalgamDeathSpeakLine TalkCmd bark, and a spine track reset) wrapped around three mechanical statements -- `HasAmalgamDied = true`, `Amalgam = null`, and `if (base.NextMove == BurnBrightForMeState) SetMoveImmediate(EnragedState)` (:230-232). The third is the divergence. C#'s SetMoveImmediate replaces the TELEGRAPHED move immediately: NextMove = EnragedState and MoveStateMachine.ForceCurrentState(EnragedState) (MonsterModel.cs:420-432), so the instant the amalgam dies the Queen's on-screen intent changes from Burn Bright For Me (BuffIntent + DefendIntent) to Enrage (BuffIntent) for the rest of that player turn. The sim has no listener for it (the sim has no MonsterModel listener category at all -- hook_dispatch G5, dormant, monsters/base.py:78-81, NOT re-verdicted here) and instead re-checks at RESOLUTION time inside the Burn Bright handler: `if self._amalgam_died(): self._enrage(ctx); return` (queen.py:169-171). Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b07.py queen-death`): with the Queen parked telegraphing Burn Bright and the amalgam then set to 0 HP, `queen STILL telegraphs: BURN_BRIGHT_FOR_ME_MOVE  intent=MoveType.BUFF` where the game would show ENRAGE_MOVE. The player therefore plans against a Defend intent the Queen will not perform, and a replay records the wrong move id for that turn. EVERYTHING DOWNSTREAM MATCHES, which is why this is an intent gap and not a whole broken phase: the same probe shows the resolved effect is Enrage's +2 Strength with 0 block, and the next telegraph is OFF_WITH_YOUR_HEAD_MOVE on both sides -- C# because ForceCurrentState parks the machine on ENRAGE_MOVE whose follow-up is OFF_WITH_YOUR_HEAD_MOVE, the sim because the machine is still on BURN_BRIGHT whose follow-up branch now takes its amalgam-dead arm. The state_log agrees too, because ForceCurrentState does not log (monster_state_machine step 34). LIVE (rule 6): 'queen' is in Glory's boss_keys (rooms.py:194), QUEEN_BOSS pairs the ported TorchHeadAmalgam with the Queen (queen.py:193-196), Burn Bright is the move she telegraphs on every turn the amalgam is alive, and killing the amalgam during the player's turn is the ordinary way the fight progresses -- both sides of the trigger are ported and the path is the fight's main line. Guarded correctly on the C# side and not needed on the sim's: SetMoveImmediate is gated on NextMove.CanTransitionAway (MonsterModel.cs:422), and BurnBrightForMeState sets no MustPerformOnceBeforeTransitioning, so the override always applies here.

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Node-by-node against Queen.cs:132-162. Six MoveStates with matching ids (PUPPET_STRINGS_MOVE / YOU_ARE_MINE_MOVE / BURN_BRIGHT_FOR_ME_MOVE / OFF_WITH_YOUR_HEAD_MOVE / EXECUTION_MOVE / ENRAGE_MOVE) and TWO ConditionalBranchStates with matching ids (YOURE_MINE_NOW_BRANCH, BURN_BRIGHT_FOR_ME_BRANCH). Wiring matches exactly: PUPPET -> YOU_ARE_MINE -> mine_branch; BURN_BRIGHT -> burn_branch; OFF_WITH_YOUR_HEAD -> EXECUTION -> ENRAGE -> OFF_WITH_YOUR_HEAD (Queen.cs:143-152 vs queen.py:138-147). Both branches carry the SAME two arms in the SAME order -- BURN_BRIGHT when the amalgam lives, OFF_WITH_YOUR_HEAD when it has died (Queen.cs:145-149 vs queen.py:140-144) -- and the duplication is deliberate on both sides. INITIAL state PUPPET_STRINGS_MOVE (Queen.cs:161 vs queen.py:151). No RandomBranchState anywhere, so there is no AddBranch integer to misread and the Queen draws no MonsterAi entropy. Intents match: CardDebuffIntent -> CARD_DEBUFF; DebuffIntent -> DEBUFF; BuffIntent + DefendIntent -> BUFF also=(DEFEND,); MultiAttackIntent(3, 5) -> ATTACK damage=3 hits=5; SingleAttackIntent(15) -> ATTACK 15; BuffIntent -> BUFF.

guards.what: HasAmalgamDied is a LATCHED flag in C# (Queen.cs:38, 60-71, 226) and a live RECOMPUTE in the sim (queen.py:111-113)
guards.rationale: C# sets the flag once, from AfterDeath, and never clears it; the sim asks `amalgam is None or amalgam.is_gone` every time a branch evaluates. Same observable in every reachable state, and the two ways they could differ were checked rather than assumed. (1) A REVIVE would unlatch the sim and not the game: the sim's three should_die implementers are IllusionPower, SteamEruptionPower and AdaptablePower and no Glory monster applies any of them to the amalgam, so no ported path takes a dead amalgam back to alive. (2) A REMOVED-BUT-ALIVE amalgam would latch the sim and not the game: `is_gone` is `is_dead or escaped` (creatures.py:43-46) and nothing in this fight escapes. C#'s own guard `base.Creature.IsAlive` at Queen.cs:223 only suppresses the latch when the Queen is already dead, which ends the combat on both sides. Concrete trigger that would make this a gap: any ported revive or escape reaching a TorchHeadAmalgam.

guards.what: BurnBrightForMeMove's teammate loop: C# iterates GetTeammatesOf with NO IsAlive filter (Queen.cs:187-191), the sim filters `not enemy.is_gone` (queen.py:176-178)
guards.issue: Queen.cs:187-188 is `CombatState.GetTeammatesOf(Creature).ToList().Where(t => t != Creature)` -- membership of the enemy side is the only test. A creature whose removal was vetoed (the death-is-not-removal case) stays on the side at 0 HP and would still be handed +1 Strength. The sim's enemies list retains every corpse, so the port must filter, and it filters on `is_gone`, which also excludes the retained corpse C# would include. SAME MECHANISM and same verdict as monster/guardbot's GuardMove target-set guard (governing rule 3). DORMANT with the trigger named: no ported power sets `retained_after_death` on a TorchHeadAmalgam, and the branch only reaches Burn Bright while the amalgam is alive anyway, so the filter cannot fire on a corpse today. The self-exclusion `t != Creature` matches the sim's `enemy is not self`.

guards.what: BurnBrightForMeMove numerics and order (Queen.cs:182-193 vs queen.py:166-179)
guards.rationale: strengthAmount = GetValueIfAscension(DeadlyEnemies, 1, 1) -> 1 = _BURN_BRIGHT_ALLY_STR; then CreatureCmd.GainBlock(Creature, 20m, ValueProp.Move) = _BURN_BRIGHT_BLOCK 20 with props=ValueProp.MOVE. The strength-to-allies loop runs BEFORE the self-block on both sides.

PuppetStrings applies ChainsOfBindingPower 3m to the targets = _PUPPET_CHAINS 3; YoureMine applies FrailPower / WeakPower / VulnerablePower 99m each, in that order (Queen.cs:177-179 vs queen.py:162-164) = _MINE_DEBUFF 99; OffWithYourHeadDamage GetValueIfAscension(DeadlyEnemies, 4, 3) -> 3 with WithHitCount(5) (and `_offWithYourHeadRepeat = 5` at Queen.cs:36 agrees) = 3 x 5; ExecutionDamage (..., 18, 15) -> 15; Enrage applies StrengthPower 2m to itself = _ENRAGE_STR 2. The three-debuff ORDER matters because each is Artifact-interceptable in turn (cmds.py:299-306) and it is preserved.
